_what: How a person's posts are kept and sent (src/social-posts.mjs). `record_type` is the kind of record a post is kept as, so a rule can watch it (set_rule when { recorded: "post" }). The link a post carries gets `link_tags` added, each a query parameter whose value is fixed (`value`) or taken from the post (`from`: post_id, platform or account_id), so a sign-up that came from a post says which post and where; `link_joiner` goes between the words and the link. `media_wait_seconds` is how long a post's video address stays readable by the place that fetches it. `outcome_states` turns each publisher outcome into the state a destination is in; `resend_states` are the states publish_post sends again by itself (never one whose outcome is unknown, which is resent only when named in resend). `outcome_words` are the plain words for a failed destination, the first row matching its retry kind or a word in its code or message; `{platform}` and `{detail}` are filled in. `publish_tool_id` is the tool a schedule runs to publish a post at its time. `voice_tools` are the Workshop tools that keep the person's writing voice (tools/how-someone-does-their-thing in Trillion-X/trillion-workshop): the tool each /posts/voice route runs (`by_field` is the input a save names who saved it in) and the tool a person's change of a draft's words is handed to. `ready_limits` are the limits a place's `format` may set on a file (src/post-ready.mjs), each the `limit` name in a media kind, the file `fact` it is compared with (byte_length, duration_seconds, or aspect: width over height), whether the fact must stay `at_most` or `at_least` the limit, the `unit` it is written in, and the fact's plain name; a new kind of limit is a row here. `ready_words` are the plain words for each thing a ready check finds, with `{platform}`, `{kind}` and the rest filled in. `calendar_max_days` is the longest span one calendar read covers.

{platform} is asking to slow down. Publish again later; the places that already have the post are not sent it again.

The words are too long for {platform}. Shorten the caption for {platform} and publish again.

not_known_words: It is not known whether {platform} took the post. Look on {platform}; if it is not there, publish again naming this account in resend.

ready_words.not_connected: This account is no longer connected. Connect it again from Connections.
ready_words.needs_media: {platform} does not post words alone. Add a video or picture.
ready_words.media_gone: This post's video or picture is no longer in your files. Choose one that is.
ready_words.kind_not_taken: {platform} does not take this kind of file ({media_type}). It takes: {kinds}.
ready_words.takes_no_files: {platform} takes words only. Leave the video or picture out of the post for {platform}.
ready_words.type_not_taken: {platform} does not take this kind of {kind} file ({media_type}). It takes: {types}.
ready_words.too_many_characters: The words for {platform} are {count} characters; it takes at most {max}. Shorten the words for {platform}.
ready_words.setting_too_long: The {name} for {platform} is {count} characters; it takes at most {max}.
ready_words.not_known: Trillion does not know the {kind}'s {fact_name}, so {platform}'s limit ({limit}) was not checked.
ready_words.all_ready: Ready for every place it is going.
ready_words.connect_places: Pick where it goes: connect {platforms} in Connections, then choose it here.
ready_words.no_places: Pick where it goes: connect a place to post in Connections.

first_contact._what: A post reaches someone when its words name them (`names`, a pattern whose first group is the handle, read over the caption and each place's own caption) or when it lists them in `reaches` (people found outside Trillion, each with where they were found). Such a post is approved only by the person, pressing Approve on their own signed-in page: an AI's approval is refused with `words.person_only` and the Posts screen as the next call. `most` people per post, `provenance_most` places each was found.

words.person_only: This post reaches {names}. A first message to someone is approved only by the person: show it to them on their Posts screen, where they read it and press Approve.
words.reaches: reaches lists the people this post contacts first (at most {most}), each { network, handle, profile_url, provenance: [{ source, url, title, posted_at }] } with at least one place they were found, as tool:find-people-outside-trillion gives them.

grounded._what: Before a first message is shown to the person, the person's own computer asks the measured decision `decision` (src/decision-evals.json, its words and the judge it is wired to) whether the message says only what was found of each person it reaches (`found`, each provenance title, joined by `joiner`) and what the person seeks of them (reaches[].sought). The answer is kept on the post as grounded; not grounded, the AI is told so in `words.not_grounded`.

words.not_grounded: Kept as a draft, but this message to {names} may say something not found in what was saved of them. Rewrite it with only what was saved and what your person seeks, before you show it to them.

hold._what: Delivery options a post may carry besides its approved content (src/social-posts.mjs): `hold_seconds` keeps a send waiting that long after publish so it can be taken back with undo_post (0 or none: sends at once), `abort_on_reply` names a conversation: when someone else writes in it after the send was armed, the send is cancelled instead of going out. Neither changes what was approved.

words.holding: Held. It goes out at {at} unless you take it back with undo_post before then.
words.still_held: It is held until {at}; undo_post takes it back before then.
words.undone: Taken back. The post is a draft again; nothing was sent. Approve it again when it is ready.
words.nothing_to_undo: {post_id} is not waiting to go out (it is {status}), so there is nothing to take back. read_post shows where it is.
words.replied: Not sent: someone wrote in the conversation after this was set to go out, so the post is a draft again. Read what they said, then approve it again if it still fits.
words.bad_seconds: hold_seconds is a whole number of seconds from 0 to {max}.
words.bad_reply: abort_on_reply is { conversation_id } of the conversation whose reply should stop the send, or null.
